---
title: Astro
description: Type-safe environment variables for Astro with the PUBLIC_ prefix.
icon: Astro
---

Use the root `zod-config` export with `clientPrefix: "PUBLIC_"`.

## Define the schema

```ts title="src/env.ts"
import { loadEnvConfig } from 'zod-config';
import { z } from 'zod';

export const env = loadEnvConfig({
  clientPrefix: 'PUBLIC_',
  server: {
    DB_PASSWORD: z.string(),
  },
  client: {
    PUBLIC_API_URL: z.url(),
  },
  runtimeEnv: import.meta.env,
});
```

Astro exposes only `PUBLIC_`-prefixed variables to client-side code. Server code (pages, endpoints, middleware) can read every variable.

## Validate when Astro starts

To stop `astro dev` and `astro build` on a missing or invalid variable, add the [`zod-config/vite` plugin](/docs/env/vite#validate-when-vite-starts) under `vite.plugins` in `astro.config.ts`:

```ts title="astro.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';
import { zodConfigEnv } from 'zod-config/vite';

export default defineConfig({
  vite: { plugins: [zodConfigEnv()] },
});
```

## Build-time and runtime values

Astro replaces `import.meta.env` values statically at build time. Because `server` variables are read from `runtimeEnv` first, passing the whole `import.meta.env` means a server value present in `.env` at build time wins over the one set at runtime. This matches what Astro's own `import.meta.env` does.

To read server variables at runtime instead, list only the client keys in `runtimeEnv`. Server values then come from `process.env`, which most Astro adapters provide:

```ts
export const env = loadEnvConfig({
  clientPrefix: 'PUBLIC_',
  server: { DB_PASSWORD: z.string() },
  client: { PUBLIC_API_URL: z.url() },
  runtimeEnv: {
    PUBLIC_API_URL: import.meta.env.PUBLIC_API_URL,
  },
});
```

For the Deno adapter, Astro's docs read variables with `Deno.env.get()` instead of `process.env`. In that case, pass the server values in `runtimeEnv` yourself.

## Astro's own `astro:env`

Astro also ships `astro:env`, a schema for environment variables declared in `astro.config` with `envField`. Use it if you only need Astro. `loadEnvConfig` is useful when you want the same Zod schemas across frameworks, or Zod features `envField` does not have.
